group_assessment.weighting: PubMed counts 2026-10-02: Chang NS[au] 138 records, 66 intersecting WWOX. A primary WWOX cell-biology laboratory (not a WWOX-DEE clinical group). In this review 18 of 54 references carry Chang NS as author; every neurodegeneration, tau, TIAF1 and in-vivo transcription-factor statement rests on those or on reviews, while the epilepsy and developmental statements rest on three independent primaries. Group experience weights its own biochemistry, not its synthesis.

multihop.note: All 54 references enumerated; the XML carries no PMIDs, so the load-bearing neurological ones were resolved by title on PubMed. Independent primaries behind the epilepsy and development sentences: refs 26 (Mallaret 2014), 27 (Abdel-Salam 2014), 48 (Suzuki 2009), each an identity record in the registries. Same-group primaries behind the neurodegeneration sentences: refs 16 (Sze 2004, mention only), 17 (Wang 2012, PAPER 056), 31 (Li 2009 sciatic injury, mention only), 40 (Lee 2010 TIAF1, no record). Ref 49 (O’Keefe 2011, Drosophila) is an identity record.

Its epilepsy and developmental sentences are already held from their primaries (PAPER 042, PAPER 043, PAPER 058). PAPER 056 cites this paper only through a lineage note. entries.proposition: In the body, the review states that in-vivo regulation of transcription factors in neuronal survival or death is not established.
entries.snippet: Whether WWOX regulates the function of transcription factors in neuronal survival or death in vivo remains to be established.
entries.anchor: WWOX in neuronal death signaling, para 1

entries.proposition: The Conclusion asserts the opposite of the body: substantial in-vivo evidence for transcription-factor control.
entries.snippet: In conclusion, substantial evidence has shown that WWOX participates in the control of the function of transcription factors in vivo.

entries.proposition: The WWOX-TIAF1 interaction is supported in this review by unpublished data from the same group.
entries.snippet: WWOX is able to interact with TIAF1 (Chang et al., unpublished)
entries.anchor: WWOX in neurological disease pathology, para 3

entries.proposition: The neurodegeneration-inhibitor statement rests on the authors’ own prior work.
entries.snippet: We have shown that WWOX is an inhibitor of neurodegeneration, because of its interaction with tau

entries.proposition: WWOX functional deficiency in Drosophila produced no neural disease phenotype.
entries.snippet: functional deficiency of WWOX in Drosophila fails to generate the disease phenotypes in the neural system
entries.anchor: WWOX in metabolic syndrome and neural development, para 3

entries.proposition: The review’s developmental conclusion is drawn from the human family, the nonsense case and the lde rat.
entries.snippet: Overall, these reports clearly indicate that germline loss-of-function of WWOX leads to developmental deficiency in the neural system.
entries.anchor: WWOX in metabolic syndrome and neural development, para 2

entries.proposition: The statement that WWOX downregulation in AD causes neuronal damage is supported only by reviews (refs 1, 2, 4).
entries.snippet: and that downregulation of WWOX in AD causes neuronal damage
entries.anchor: WWOX in metabolic syndrome and neural development, para 3
